verdict.justification: Deliverable A is much stronger because it builds a dynamic spreadsheet using Excel formulas (`SUM`, `SUMIF`, `SUMIFS`, `ROUNDUP`) and includes the requested email to the plant manager (`Email to Plant Manager.txt`). In contrast, Deliverable B hardcodes every single value in the main planning sheet without using any formulas, which is poor spreadsheet practice for a production plan. Furthermore, Deliverable A notices the ambiguity in the template between cell A46 ('Team Member Labor Total (Minutes Rounded Up Whole)') and cell B47 ('Total Hours'), sensibly updating B47 to 'Total Minutes' so the values match the section instruction. Deliverable B leaves the header as 'Total Hours' and puts decimal hours (`9.800000000000001` and `11.08`), violating the 'Minutes Rounded Up Whole' rule. Although Deliverable A adds two helper columns (L and M) on Sheet1 to allow `SUMIFS` to calculate the daily press totals dynamically, this is a very practical modeling choice and is clearly documented in its assumptions.
